item.title: [机器人] 英伟达上线SimReady仿真资产库
item.author: @CyberRobooo
item.description:
CyberRobo称英伟达推出SimReady Central，提供3500余个开放OpenUSD资产（含FANUC/UR机械臂、Robotiq夹爪等），并强调经真实硬件校准的碰撞、质量、摩擦与关节限位物理质检。

@CyberRobooo · 赞 15 · 转 6 · 浏览 738

This is huge. NVIDIA just launched SimReady Central: 3,500+ open OpenUSD assets, from FANUC and UR arms to Robotiq grippers and LG appliances. Most of them trace back to one team,@LightwheelAI . The important part is physics QA. Collision, mass, friction and joint limits are calibrated against real hardware. Without that, a 3D model can look right while teaching a robot contacts that don't exist. Lightwheel also packages assets with explicit profiles, validation requirements and hash manifests, then adapts the physics for PhysX, Newton and MuJoCo. That’s the harder work: making assets reliable and reusable across simulation engines, instead of forcing every robot team to rebuild and revalidate them. If this scales, teams can spend less time preparing simulations and more time training and testing robots.

item.title: [AI] Anthropic联合创始人回应METR报告
item.author: @Sam_McCandlish
item.description:
Anthropic联合创始人Sam McCandlish称已向METR提供未发布模型基准等内部数据供其独立评估；他认同AI在加速自家研究，并预告数周内将发布Anthropic自身的进度与安全举措分析。

@Sam_McCandlish · 赞 1617 · 转 128 · 浏览 173206

I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months. I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals. The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work. How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate. For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions. Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further. This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one. We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here. In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

item.title: [AI] 开源Hyperkernel加速GPU推理
item.author: @hyperstition_cc
item.description:
Hyperstition发布递归megakernel生成器Hyperkernel，称在DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM推理、预训练、机器人与FSD等11个领域达到SOTA，并开源相关megakernel与后续完整栈。

@hyperstition_cc · 赞 326 · 转 42 · 浏览 28696

We invented a recursive megakernel generator called Hyperkernel, the most complete solution to megakernels and GPU efficiency. Hyperkernel-generated megakernels achieve state of the art performance on 11 different domains: inference (DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM), pretraining (Qwen), hardware fault recovery, robotics (π₀-FAST, ACT) diffusion and real time world models (Matrix-Game), full self driving (OpenPilot), voice models (Moshi), genomics (Evo 2) and protein folding (ESMFold). All of this in a single kernel launch. For context, Hyperkernel generated fully optimized megakernels for robotics, genomics and voice in under 50 minutes, and doubled the efficiency for >5 models generally using only about 60-100 lines of code per megakernel. This speaks to the unparalleled standard for code quality in the automated generations. Our first release today open sources the megakernels themselves. Over the next couple weeks, we will release the entire Hyperkernel stack, along with the complete serving stack for Kimi and GLM (20-30% inference efficiency gains across all concurrencies). item.title: [机器人] RoboColosseum真实机器人评测上线
item.author: @TheHumanoidHub
item.description:
RoboColosseum在真实硬件上盲测机器人策略，覆盖150多场景并公开含失败在内的全部rollout；已测OpenAI、Anthropic、NVIDIA等30余策略，学术实验室可获1万小时免费评测。

@TheHumanoidHub · 赞 14 · 转 3 · 浏览 2288

Robotics finally has its real-world arena. RoboColosseum is a real-world benchmark that tests robot policies on hundreds of actual robots across 150+ scenes, not cherry-picked demos. You bring a model, they run it blind on real hardware and publish every rollout (failures included) on Hugging Face. Two ways models are tested: - Open track: two unnamed models get the same brand-new instruction in the same scene. A human judge watches both runs and picks the winner, or a tie. Think LMArena, but on real robots. It measures zero-shot performance on novel tasks. - Fine-tune track: every model is fine-tuned on one fixed task from the same open-source demos, then gets 25 attempts. An apples-to-apples test of how well a model learns a specific skill. Over 30 policies from OpenAI, Anthropic, NVIDIA, Galaxea, Ai2 and more are tested across Unitree G1, Franka, YAM and SO-101. Why it matters: across 20,000+ real runs, no model won everywhere. Rankings flipped depending on the task and the robot body. That's the whole point: a single demo or benchmark tells you almost nothing about what a policy can actually do. This is the field finally getting honest, real robots, in the wild, every failure published. And 10,000 eval hours are free for academic labs. https://t.co/bRNf0LcD9R
